tei:titleStmt.tei:title: The Announcement of the New Month on Shabbat Mevorkhim, per the Old Romaniote Rite

tei:div.tei:head: The Announcement of the New Month on Shabbat Mevorkhim, per the Old Romaniote Rite

tei:l.tei:note: On the sabbath before a new moon, the prayer leader holds the Torah scroll and says:

tei:lg.tei:l: May the Cause, God of Israel,
in Their vast compassion and great and sweet mercies,
gaze from Their abode
upon Their Temple
and upon Their Palace,
and shake it out of its ashes,
and establish it from its destruction,
and build it a glorious building,
an improved building,
a building that will not be destroyed
or shattered ever, in our days,
and in the days of all the house of Israel,
and say amen.
As it is written:
Built, I have built, a house of resplendence for You,
an abode for Your dwelling eternally. (I Kings 8:13)
And it is written:
Again I will build you,
and you will be built again, virgin Israel!
Again will you don your hand-drums
and go out in the players’ dance. (Jeremiah 31:4)
And it is written:
Thus says the Cause:
Hey, I will return the exile of Jacob’s tents,
and have compassion on his lodgings,
and the city will be built on its ruin-mound,
and the palace on justice be set. (Jeremiah 30:18)
And it is written:
And they will build houses
and dwell in them,
and plant vineyards
and eat their fruit. (Isaiah 65:21)
And it is written:
They will not build for another to dwell in,
they will not plant for another to eat from,
for like the days of a tree shall be My people’s days,
and My chosen ones will use up their own handiwork. (Isaiah 65:22)
And it is written:
They will not toil purposelessly,
nor bear children for dismay,
for a Cause-blessed seed are they,
and their descendants with them. (Isaiah 65:23)
And it is written:
And before they even call
I will answer them;
while they are speaking
I will hear. (Isaiah 65:24)
And it is written:
And the children of Israel’s number will be like the sand of the sea,
which cannot be measured nor counted,
and instead of being said of them “No people of Mine are you!,”
of them will be said “the children of the living Deity.” (Hosea 2:1)
And it is written:
And on that day, the great shofar will be blasted,
and those lost in the land of Assyria
and exiled in the land of Egypt
will come and bow to the Cause
on the holy mountain in Jerusalem. (Isaiah 27:13)
And it is written:
And the Cause will be sovereign over all the earth;
on that day the Cause will be one
and Their name will be one. (Zechariah 14:9)
And it is written:
And at the end of days,
the mountain of the Cause’s house will be set right as head of mountains,
highest of hills,
and all the nations will stream towards it. (Isaiah 2:2)
And it is written:
And many peoples will go and say,
“Come on, let’s go to the Cause’s mountain,
to the house of Jacob’s God,
to be taught from Their ways,
so we may go by Their paths!”
For out of Zion will come Teaching,
and the Cause’s word from Jerusalem. (Isaiah 2:3)
And it is written:
And They will judge between nations
and arbitrate for many peoples,
and they will beat their swords to plowshares
and their spears into pruning-hooks;
no longer shall nation raise sword against nation,
nor will they again learn war. (Isaiah 2:4)
And it is written:
House of Jacob, come on,
so we may walk in the Cause’s light! (Isaiah 2:5)
And it is written:
And hey, the glory of Israel’s God,
coming from the eastern way,
its sound like the sound of vast waters,
and the earth was enlightened by Their glory. (Ezekiel 43:2)
Thus may the Cause of Forces enlighten us
and all Their people the house of Israel,
and say amen.
Hark! All the people,
pay attention to hear the sound of the sanctification of this month,
as our masters and rabbis of the holy assembly
who were living in the land of Israel established:
we have the new month of [month name]
on [such-and-such a day or days] of the week,
its calculation and its enumeration on [such-and-such a day] of the week.
May the Sovereign of Existence make it a good sign for us
and all Their people the house of Israel,
and say amen!

tei:note.tei:p: It is unclear what the difference between the first and second entailed weekdays here are, and the maḥzor lacks explanation. One possibility is that the former is the day or days of Rosh Ḥodesh as it is observed, while the latter is the day of the molad — which is not always on Rosh Ḥodesh itself. However, the oldest known record of the custom of announcing the molad is from the siddur of the ShLa”H, two centuries after the Romaniote maḥzor was printed. Another possibility, suggested in personal communication from Nathan Kasimer, is that the former is the day or days of Rosh Ḥodesh, while the latter is the actual first day of the month, to remind the community that the first day of the month is the second day of a two-day Rosh Ḥodesh.
